nfl.oneThing: Jalen Hurts is out for the Eagles' game against the Panthers in London after a superficial blood clot was found in his calf.

headlines.title: Hurts out in London with a blood clot in his calf
headlines.summary: The Eagles have ruled Jalen Hurts out for Sunday's game against the Panthers because of a superficial blood clot in his calf. The team says Hurts first sought treatment for the calf on October 8, after an injury he picked up in the October 4 game against the Rams. He practised in full before an ultrasound on Saturday found the clot. Doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded he should not play.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia are 2-3 and on a three-game losing streak, so losing their starter for a game in London makes a hard stretch harder.

headlines.title: Commanders take the blame for the overtime clock mistake
headlines.summary: Washington let the clock run out while in field goal range during a Week 5 overtime game against the Giants. Coach Dan Quinn and quarterback Jayden Daniels have both taken responsibility. Daniels defended Quinn and said the failure was his, calling it 'a failure'. Quinn said the team has turned the page from that game.
headlines.whyItMatters: Washington are 1-3-1 in the NFC East, behind the 3-1-1 Giants, so every mistake in close games costs them.

headlines.title: Jonathan Taylor isn't worried about a slow start
headlines.summary: His 3.9 yards per rush is well below his career average of 4.8. His third-down conversion rate of 33.3% is also below his career mark of 47.3%. He is still in the top 10 in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns, but he has yet to post a 100-yard rushing game this season.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Colts are 2-3 and host the winless Titans, and they need Taylor to become a big-play threat again.

headlines.title: Ravens without Lamar Jackson
headlines.summary: Lamar Jackson missed Thursday's practice with an ankle injury, and the Ravens listed him as a non-participant. Receiver Zay Flowers was added to the injury report as a limited participant with a toe problem. The Ravens' game without Jackson against the Falcons averaged 17 million viewers.
headlines.whyItMatters: Baltimore are 4-1 and second in the AFC, so how they cope without Jackson will test their depth.

teamNews.title: Jeanty says he's ready for the Bills
teamNews.text: Ashton Jeanty says he feels great after his ankle and foot problems, and coach Klint Kubiak says he's playing. Jeanty missed practice last Friday with a flare-up of plantar fasciitis. He had 27 yards on 10 carries in the loss to New England, his worst rushing game of the season.

contextCard.title: How practice squad elevations work
contextCard.body: Teams can add players from the practice squad to the active roster for a game, which is called an elevation. The player is paid for that game and then returns to the practice squad. The rules limit how often a team can do this with the same player during a season.

nba.oneThing: The NBA's GM survey made the Spurs the title favourites, with 50% of the votes, and Victor Wembanyama the favourite for MVP.

headlines.title: GMs make the Spurs title favourites and Wemby their pick
headlines.summary: The annual NBA general manager survey has the Spurs as title favourites, with 50% of the votes, narrowly ahead of the Thunder. Victor Wembanyama received 93% of the votes when GMs were asked who they would sign to start a franchise, up from 83% a year ago and a survey record. He was also picked as the heavy favourite for MVP with 77% of the votes and was projected to be the league's best defensive player. The Spurs won 62 games last season and lost to the Knicks in the Finals.
headlines.whyItMatters: Expectations are now high, and the GMs still gave the Thunder support, so San Antonio will have to prove it on the court.

headlines.title: Thunder top the early power ratings, Spurs second
headlines.summary: Yahoo's preseason power ratings have the Thunder first at +8.1, the Spurs second at +7.4 and Boston third at +4.8. The ratings use regular-season win totals, title odds, injury news and the first few games priced, with a manual adjustment on top. Home court is worth 3 points in this system.
headlines.whyItMatters: The ratings are a forecast, not a result, and the Spurs are rated close to the Thunder at the top.

headlines.title: Lakers, Bucks and Grizzlies have to trim before Monday
headlines.summary: Teams must be down to 15 contracts by the end of Monday. Yahoo reports that the Lakers, Bucks and Grizzlies still have more than that and are reportedly exploring trades.
headlines.whyItMatters: The trades and waivers over the next few days will set the final rosters that open each team's season.

headlines.title: The Clippers' turbulent era officially ends
headlines.summary: The Clippers have been through a turbulent year. They were featured at least ten times on Pablo Torre Finds Out over the Aspiration saga and were under NBA investigation for circumventing the salary cap. Their punishment was the loss of five first-round picks, and owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for a year. They also traded James Harden, Ivica Zubac and Kawhi Leonard, and used the fifth overall pick on Keaton Wagler.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Clippers are building a new group around players like Wagler, and the next few seasons will show whether the rebuild works.

headlines.title: Maxey says a healthy Embiid 'changes everything'
headlines.summary: Tyrese Maxey says a healthy Joel Embiid changes everything for the 76ers. Embiid has never played 82 games and has averaged just 49 games a season across his 10-year career. He played 38 games last season, managing right hip complications, left knee issues and appendicitis. Philadelphia has added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, and the GMs in the survey were unsure about the 76ers.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia's season depends heavily on whether Embiid stays on the court with its new stars.

teamNews.text: NBC Sports' Perloff says the Spurs need more size around Wembanyama. Pounding The Rock argues that Tarris Reed gives the Spurs the backup-centre plan they lacked last season, after Luke Kornet struggled as the playoffs went on.

recaps.keyLine: Bouyea 15 pts, 4 reb, 8 ast · Dunn 15 pts, 2 reb, 0 ast · Wembanyama 19 pts, 4 reb, 3 ast, 4 blk · Castle 18 pts, 4 reb, 3 ast
recaps.text: The Spurs beat the Suns 123–103 at home for their first preseason win after starting 0-3. Victor Wembanyama had 19 points and four blocks, Stephon Castle added 18 and Carter Bryant had 16. The game also gave the first look at a three-guard lineup of De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Castle, which is worth watching as the season starts.

recaps.keyLine: Porter Jr. 27 pts, 1 reb, 1 ast · Demin 17 pts, 3 reb, 3 ast · Antetokounmpo 20 pts, 15 reb, 9 ast, 3 blk · Wiggins 19 pts, 6 reb, 1 ast
recaps.text: Miami beat Brooklyn 144–128 in an upset, after the Nets had been unbeaten at 3-0. Giannis Antetokounmpo had 20 points, 15 rebounds, nine assists and three blocks, and Andrew Wiggins scored 19. Michael Porter Jr. had 27 points for Brooklyn, but it was not enough.

recaps.text: The Clippers beat the Nuggets 122–110. Darius Garland had seven assists and 14 points, and Rui Hachimura added 16 points and five rebounds. Trevon Brazile led Denver with 22 points, while Cam Whitmore had 17.

recaps.keyLine: Fears 16 pts, 3 reb, 5 ast, 3 stl · Matkovic 11 pts, 2 reb, 0 ast · Lawal 16 pts, 4 reb, 0 ast · Poulakidas 16 pts, 3 reb, 0 ast
recaps.text: New Orleans beat Dallas 101–97 in a close game. Jeremiah Fears had 16 points, five assists and three steals for the Pelicans. Tobi Lawal and John Poulakidas each scored 16 for the Mavericks, who finished with a 1-2 record.

recaps.text: Chicago beat Milwaukee 125–104. Matas Buzelis had 19 points and five threes, and Leonard Miller added 18 points and seven rebounds. Kam Jones scored 23 for the Bucks, and Brayden Burries had 19 points, five rebounds, five assists and four steals in the loss.
